name: openrouter-status
purpose: POST /api/backends/chat-completions/status for the OPENROUTER source, a different branch of the same pinned matrix: GET urlJoin(apiUrl, "/models") with the Authorization header plus OPENROUTER_HEADERS, and the provider body passed through unchanged.
stage1Boundary: Stage 1 validates the backend -> provider transformation only. Browser-side prompt assembly happens in the frontend before the request reaches the route and is NOT covered here; a green provider-wire capture is not evidence of preset-level equivalence.

tier2.reason: The mock listens on an ephemeral loopback port, so the authority is not a property of either backend. Justified by tools/mock-provider listening on port 0.
tier2.harnessSource: tools/mock-provider/main.go: --port 0 asks the kernel for a free port, so the authority is not stable

tier2.rule: value replaced with Bearer <redacted>, presence and scheme preserved
tier2.reason: The scenario supplies a synthetic key; the header's presence and scheme are the contract, the value is not.

tier2.rule: the recorder origin is replaced with <mock>
tier2.reason: OPENROUTER has NO reverse_proxy and NO custom_url: chat-completions.js:2302 is the hardcoded literal https://openrouter.ai/api/v1, so the pinned leg can only reach the recorder through the probe transport redirect and the Go leg through its seam. The PATH (/api/v1/chat/completions) is untouched and IS compared, which is the part the pinned literal decides.

tier3.reason: It is a measurement of elapsed wall-clock time, so it differs on every run and no backend can match it; the value is a duration, not a contract.
